court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2022 and have a child aged about 18 years. The petitioner is seeking to transfer the divorce case filed by the respondent from the Subordinate Court, Ottanchathiram to Udumalapet due to her inability to travel for the trial.

legal_principles.principle: Maintenance is the livelihood for a child, and even in cases where the wife is employed, the father has to contribute his share of maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The maintenance is the livelihood for a child and even in cases, the wife is employed, the father has to contribute his share of maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: Interim maintenance is to be granted whenever a child is to be maintained by the parents, considering the status, income, lifestyle and other mitigating factors.
legal_principles.held: The remedy of interim maintenance is a measure of social justice as envisaged under the Constitution to prevent the children from falling into destitution and vagrancy.

legal_principles.principle: The courts cannot keep maintenance petitions pending for a prolonged period and should grant interim maintenance soon after the filing of the petition.
legal_principles.held: The Courts cannot keep such maintenance petitions have a prolonged period and in all such petitions, soon after the filing of the same, interim maintenance is to be granted considering the status, income, lifestyle and other mitigating factors.

outcome.final_order: The petition for transfer is allowed and the HMOP No.185 of 2022 is transferred from the file of the Subordinate Court, Ottanchathiram to the file of the Subordinate Court, Udumalapet.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: advising on transfer of cases between courts
